words.gloss: to those who bale out water

ai.literal: I would indeed hide, I, this pain; to those who bale out, spring-water like, it increases.
ai.translation: I would indeed hide this pain of mine, but like a spring that wells up more and more as water is drawn, it only increases.
ai.modern: நான் இந்தத் துன்பத்தை மறைக்கவே நினைக்கிறேன்; ஆனால், இறைக்க இறைக்க ஊறும் ஊற்றுநீரைப் போல இது மேலும் மேலும் அதிகமாகிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine describes the overwhelming nature of her love-sickness during separation. She wishes to conceal her suffering from others to preserve her modesty, but her efforts are futile. She compares her pain to a natural spring: just as drawing water from a spring causes more water to gush forth, her attempts to suppress or drain her feelings only make them increase and overflow.

ai.literal: Even concealing I cannot bear this affliction; telling to him who caused the affliction also brings shame.
ai.translation: I cannot bear to conceal this painful affliction, yet telling it to the one who caused it only brings me shame.
ai.modern: இந்தத் துன்பத்தை என்னால் மறைக்கவும் முடியவில்லை; இந்தத் துன்பத்தைத் தந்தவரிடம் இதைச் சொல்வதும் எனக்கு வெட்கத்தைத் தருகிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine expresses her deep inner conflict of love-sickness. She is unable to hide the pain of separation any longer as it overwhelms her. However, revealing her suffering to her lover, who is the very cause of her pain, feels deeply embarrassing and brings her shame. The couplet beautifully captures the delicate struggle between unbearable emotional pain and the preservation of one's modesty.

ai.literal: And desire and modesty, life not protecting, hang inside my unable to bear body.
ai.translation: Within my body, which is unable to bear the pain, desire and modesty hang like a balanced load, leaving my life unprotected.
ai.modern: தாங்க முடியாத என் உடம்பினுள்ளே, உயிரைக் காக்காமல், காமமும் நாணமும் இரு பக்கமும் தொங்கிக் கொண்டிருக்கின்றன.
ai.explanation: The heroine describes her intense internal conflict using the metaphor of a shoulder-pole (kāvadi). Her desire (kāmam) pulls her toward her lover, while her modesty (nāṇam) holds her back. These two opposing forces hang like heavy weights on either side of her fragile body, which is unable to bear the strain. As a result of this constant tug-of-war, her life remains unprotected and hangs precariously in the balance.

ai.literal: The ocean of desire indeed exists; to swim across that, the protective raft indeed is not there.
ai.translation: The ocean of desire indeed exists; but the protective raft to swim across it does not.
ai.modern: காமமாகிய கடல் நிச்சயமாக இருக்கிறது; ஆனால் அதைக் கடந்து நீந்துவதற்குப் பாதுகாப்பான தோணி நிச்சயமாக இல்லை.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine compares her overwhelming desire and grief of separation to a vast, endless ocean. While this ocean of passion is very real and present, she laments that she lacks the safety raft—her lover's presence or comfort—needed to cross it. The word 'mannum' is used twice as an emphatic particle to contrast the absolute certainty of the ocean's existence with the absolute certainty of the raft's absence. This vivid metaphor highlights her complete helplessness in the face of love-sickness.

ai.literal: In enmity, what will they become indeed, I wonder, the arrival of sorrow within love who cause?
ai.translation: If those who are in a loving relationship cause only the arrival of sorrow, what would they become if they were to turn into enemies?
ai.modern: அன்பான உறவிலேயே துன்பம் வருவதற்குக் காரணமாக இருப்பவர்கள், ஒருவேளை பகைமை கொண்டால் என்னவாக மாறுவார்களோ?
ai.explanation: The heroine, suffering from the pain of separation, laments the behavior of her lover. She points out that even during their intimate relationship, he brings her immense grief through his absence. She wonders aloud what kind of suffering he would inflict if he were to become an open enemy. The word 'tuppu' is chosen here in its sense of 'enmity' to contrast with 'naṭpu' (love), highlighting the irony of receiving pain from a loved one.

ai.literal: Pleasure is an ocean; but love, when that afflicts, the pain is greater than that.
ai.translation: The pleasure of love is as vast as an ocean; but when that same love afflicts, its pain is far greater than the ocean.
ai.modern: காமத்தின் இன்பம் கடல் போன்றது; ஆனால், அக்காமுற்ற நெஞ்சம் துன்புறுத்தும்போது, அதன் துன்பம் அக்கடலை விடப் பெரியதாகும்.
ai.explanation: The heroine compares the dual experiences of love to the vastness of an ocean. She notes that the joy of love is as boundless as the sea. However, when love begins to torment her due to separation, the resulting grief becomes even larger than that immense ocean. The contrast highlights how the intensity of suffering in love can easily overwhelm even its greatest pleasures.

parts.gloss: I do not (first-person singular negative suffix)

ai.literal: Desire's fierce flood swimming, shore I do not see; even at midnight, I indeed am awake.
ai.translation: Swimming in the fierce flood of desire, I cannot see the shore; even in the dead of night, I am left all alone, awake.
ai.modern: காமம் என்னும் கொடிய வெள்ளத்தில் நீந்தியும் அதன் கரையை நான் காணவில்லை; நள்ளிரவிலும் நான் ஒருவளே விழித்திருக்கிறேன்.
ai.explanation: The heroine describes her overwhelming suffering during separation. She compares her intense passion to a fierce, rushing flood (கடும்புனல்) in which she is drowning. Though she struggles and swims (நீந்தி) constantly, she cannot find any shore (கரை காணேன்) or relief. To intensify her grief, even during the dead of night (யாமத்தும்) when the rest of the world is asleep, she alone remains awake (யானே உளேன்) with her painful thoughts.

ai.literal: Enduring living beings all having made to sleep, showing mercy, the night, except me, does not have a companion.
ai.translation: Having put all living beings to sleep and comforted them, the night has no companion left but me.
ai.modern: நிலைபெற்ற உயிர்கள் எல்லாவற்றையும் தூங்கச் செய்து அவற்றுக்கு அருள் புரியும் இந்த இரவுக்கு, என்னைத் தவிர வேறு துணை இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The heroine, suffering from the intense pain of separation, is unable to sleep. She looks around and realizes that the night has kindly put all other living creatures to sleep, granting them peaceful rest. Since everyone else is asleep, only she and the night remain awake in the darkness. She poetically expresses that the night, too, is lonely and has found no companion other than her to share its long hours.

ai.literal: Than the cruelty of the cruel one, themselves cruel, these days, long, passing, the nights.
ai.translation: More cruel than the cruelty of my cruel lover are these nights, which stretch out so long and refuse to pass.
ai.modern: கொடுமை செய்யும் காதலரின் கொடுமையை விட, இந்த நாட்களில் மிக நீண்டு கழிகின்ற இரவுகள் தாமே அதிகக் கொடுமையானவை ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: The heroine, suffering in separation, compares two sources of pain: her absent lover and the night. She calls her lover 'koṭiyār' (the cruel one) for leaving her, but finds that the nights ('irā') during this separation are even more cruel ('tām koṭiya') than his actions. These nights stretch out endlessly ('neṭiya kaḻiyum') and refuse to end, making her loneliness and longing feel infinite.

words.gloss: to the place where he is

ai.literal: Like the mind, to the place where he is, if they could go, in a flood of water, swim they would not, alas, my eyes.
ai.translation: If my eyes could only travel to the place where my beloved is, just as my mind does, they would not have to swim in this flood of tears.
ai.modern: என் நெஞ்சத்தைப் போல, என் காதலர் இருக்கும் இடத்திற்கு என் கண்களும் செல்ல முடியுமானால், அவை இந்த வெள்ளப் பெருக்கான கண்ணீரில் நீந்த வேண்டியிருக்காது.
ai.explanation: The heroine laments her state of separation, where her eyes constantly weep. She notes that her mind has the ability to instantly travel to where her beloved resides. If only her eyes could do the same and go to that place, they would be gazing upon him instead of crying. Consequently, they would not have to swim in a flood of their own tears. The particles 'மன்னோ' express her deep regret and longing.
